name: Los Cabos International Airport
before:
The gateway to Los Cabos, 10 km north of San José del Cabo at the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula. It handled 7,529,900 passengers in 2025, sixth busiest in Mexico and fourth for international passengers.

The traffic is overwhelmingly North American. Most United States and Canadian mainline carriers treat this as a destination airport, and it also sits on the busy corridor between the Baja California Peninsula and mainland Mexico. More than 50 destinations are served across the Americas and Europe.

There are two terminals, split domestic and international rather than by airline. Terminal 1 handles domestic flights from a single storey building of 16,580 square metres, with eight gates on the ground level that passengers walk out to, plus a VIP lounge on a mezzanine.

The single runway is 3,000 metres, with apron space for 22 narrow bodied aircraft and the ability to take wide bodies.

Note there is a second, much smaller airport in the region. Cabo San Lucas International is about 26 km south, so check which one a ticket names.
after:
The main airport for Los Cabos, 11 km north of San José del Cabo, near the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula. It handled 7,529,900 passengers in 2025.

Most were on international flights, 62 per cent by the count of GAP, which runs the airport. GAP names its main destinations as Mexico City, Los Angeles, Guadalajara, Dallas-Fort Worth and Tijuana. Its main airlines, the operator says, are Volaris, Viva, American, Alaska and United. Flights reach more than 50 destinations across the Americas and Europe.

Terminal 1 takes domestic flights and Terminal 2 international ones.

The single runway is 3,000 metres.

A second, smaller airport, Cabo San Lucas International, lies to the south west, so check which one a ticket names.

claims.claim: Terminal 1 takes domestic flights and Terminal 2 international ones
claims.inAfter: Terminal 1 takes domestic flights and Terminal 2 international ones.
claims.note: Was 'There are two terminals, split domestic and international rather than by airline'. Both sources agree that Terminal 1 takes the domestic flights and Terminal 2 the international ones ('only' is GAP's word alone, so it is left out); GAP's page adds that Terminal 1 also takes some international flights, which is why 'rather than by airline' is cut. The terminal count is not stated: GAP's undated page still says three terminals and a Terminal 4 under construction, while Wikipedia says the old Terminal 3 was merged into Terminal 2 between 2018 and 2020 and there are now two. GAP's current plans are to enlarge Terminal 2, with automated migration gates (held back below).
